judgements.decision: The corrective path: prepare, the settle that leaves a task unresolved, and the settle of the correction. Counted to the correction that settles. A task is unresolved when its verification fails, or when its claim reports it as failed, blocked or skipped. The Exarchos calls are the same for each cause. The fixer is the harness call of a failed task. A blocked or skipped task takes another harness step, which the count does not show. Settlement compiles no capsule on this path, so no prepare follows. Landing, the backstop and the transition then follow as on the normal path. Reading the receipt of the halted segment names no call. A summary that omits unresolved entries claims every required task in the same call. A receipt that also carries a design revision prepares first, which is the material-revision path. A second correction is a re-run that the prose names with no call site and no limit, so the count is a lower bound.
judgements.subject: a task is unresolved after settlement, so a fixer is dispatched and the task is settled in a new batch on the same capsule

judgements.decision: fresh fixer dispatch to the worktree of the unresolved task

judgements.decision: A request error only: a fault in the shape of a claim, a rationale that names a decision that the capsule does not delegate, a deviation that cannot be held, or a refused deviation. Counted to the corrected request that settles. The correction is to the request, so no fixer is dispatched: a task that fails its verification is the corrective-capsule path. A refused deviation whose rework task leaves the plan prepares again first, which is the normal path. Landing, the backstop and the transition follow as on the normal path.

judgements.decision: The stale path: prepare, the settle that finds the capsule stale, the second prepare, and the settle under its capsule. Nothing was verified under the stale batch. The second prepare and its settle have no call site of their own, because each is the call that the normal path already shows, so each is counted at that site. Dispatching a named task again from the new packet is a harness call that the branch does not name, so the harness count is a lower bound. The revision that made the capsule stale belongs to another batch, and its calls are not counted here. Landing, the backstop and the transition follow as on the normal path.

judgements.decision: The decision is recorded as its own fact on that call, and an accepted one verifies the held work and settles the batch, after which landing and the transition follow as on the normal path. An accepted one that leaves a task unresolved goes on to the correction of the corrective-capsule path, one call more. The task is unresolved after a failed verification, or because its held claim reports it as not completed. A rejected one rejects the batch, and the settle of the corrected work is the settlement-rejected path. An accepted deviation of a material kind also records a design revision on that call. The design-revised path counts to that call, and the material-revision path counts the continuation that follows it.

judgements.decision: Counted to the call that records the revision. The revision is recorded on the decision call, so this path adds that call and no other. A revision names only unfinished tasks: a task outside the batch, or a task that the batch reports as not completed. Those tasks wait for the next capsule version whatever the round's verdict. What follows the revision, the continuation prepare and the settle of the capsule it compiles, is the material-revision path and is counted there, not here. A batch that arrives on a capsule that a later revision made stale prepares a second time. The recompile-required path counts that, not this one.
judgements.subject: an accepted deviation revises the design, so the tasks the orchestrator named as affected wait for the next capsule version

judgements.decision: the decision round: accepting a deviation of a material kind records the design revision on this same call
judgements.subject: exarchos_orchestrate.settle

judgements.decision: The whole path of a material deviation with a human decision, counted to the settlement of the recompiled capsule: prepare, the settle that is held, the settle that carries the decision and records the revision, the continuation prepare, and the settle of the capsule it compiled. The continuation and its settle have no call site of their own, because each is the call the normal path already shows, so each is counted at that site. The design-revised path stops at the decision call; this path counts on from it. The own-task path has the same five calls: the held batch reports a task as blocked and its deviation names that task, the decision round needs a correction and records the revision, and the continuation compiles the task. Dispatching and collecting the recompiled tasks are harness calls the branch does not name again, so the harness count is a lower bound. Landing, the backstop and the transition follow as on the normal path. An invalidated task that is not ready yet waits for a later prepare, which is the normal path. A retry of the continuation replays its receipt and is not a second continuation.

loops.prs: pull requests in one synthesized stack

method: Call sites are located by spelling, never hand-listed: call expressions, backtick spans naming a tool and a verb, a tool beside an action key, bare action keys resolved to the one tool that serves the name, harness-call placeholders, and fenced shell blocks.
Tool names and the action roster come from the registry snapshot. A counted call the roster does not serve is refused, not counted.

Which path a located site belongs to is a recorded judgement anchored to text in its source. Every located site must be placed on a path or excluded with a reason, so a new call cannot be silently ignored and a removed one cannot silently count as zero.
Where the prose names a loop, a call is counted per task or per pull request and reported as a formula. Where it names none, the call is counted once.

Exception paths count only the calls their branch names. A branch that re-invokes the skill adds the normal path again. Re-runs the prose does not name are not counted, so exception counts are lower bounds.
A fetched runbook is expanded in place only when the skill says to execute its steps. Otherwise its steps are compared with the prose path and every difference is reported.
describe and runbook calls are Exarchos MCP calls, counted apart from work calls. Harness calls are counted apart and are in no Exarchos total.

scope.counted: Exarchos MCP calls and harness calls spelled out in each SKILL.md body, plus the steps of the runbooks those bodies say to execute.
scope.lowerBound: The references/ files a SKILL.md names are not read. A call whose only recipe lives there is not counted, so every path here is a lower bound on what the full skill tree prescribes.
